action: Verify WinRAR and other tools on your network are the publisher's signed copies; apply application allowlisting and code-signing checks, and alert on memory that is read, write and execute at once and on PNGs with truncated headers.
exec: Trusted programs can be rewritten into malware carriers whose fingerprint changes every run, so hash-based blocking is weak.
plain: Security firm ReversingLabs describes BubbleLoader, malware that edits ordinary programs like WinRAR so they secretly load other malware, and changes its fingerprint every time it runs.

key_findings: BubbleLoader patches the entry point of a benign program and appends two PNG files; the host then decrypts and reflectively loads a final payload in memory.
Hosts seen include WinRAR, x64dbg, Windows Media Player, a Firefox launcher and virtiofs; the post names no victims or sectors and the final payload varies by sample.
Earliest samples date from February 2026, with two activity clusters in mid-September and early October.

It overwrites padding bytes in the payload with timestamp-derived randomness on each run, so the in-memory hash changes every execution, and hooks RtlPcToFileHeader in ntdll so the payload can handle exceptions.
The second PNG is a fake with a truncated header, which ReversingLabs offers as a static detection signal; the post does not say how the altered programs reach victims.
recommendations: Enforce strict application allowlisting and code-signing verification, especially for common utilities such as WinRAR.
Have EDR alert on read-write-execute memory allocated with VirtualAlloc and on protection changes to the ntdll routine RtlPcToFileHeader.
Add static rules for embedded PNGs with a truncated header.
Rely on behavioural memory analysis and entry-point integrity checks, not only static payload hashes.

summary: ReversingLabs analysed BubbleLoader, a loader that rewrites a few instructions at a program's entry point and adds two PNG images to turn legitimate software, including WinRAR and Windows Media Player, into a carrier for other malware. It changes its payload's in-memory hash on every run. Samples date from February 2026, with activity clusters in September and October. Delivery method is not stated.
title: ReversingLabs: BubbleLoader turns WinRAR and other programs into malware carriers
